A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OffTopicEval study and provide readable methods, equations, results, figures, and Appendices A–Q. Content can be reliably matched despite reflow and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of open- and closed-weight LLMs, mitigation experiments, and appendix analyses of prompt design, multi-turn behavior, and parameter steering.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and appendix analyses, with revised activation-steering results in Table 8.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction procedure, P-ground and Q-ground prompts, activation-steering procedure, and appendix LoRA method are unchanged. Revised Table 8 values do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 21 assistant scenarios, MMLU/Global MMLU coverage, English/Chinese/Hindi evaluation, and direct and adaptive OOD tests. The additional enterprise-risk discussion introduces no evaluated task or population.

E2.justification: The evaluated model and mitigation comparator sets are unchanged. The open- and closed-weight prompt-steering tables exchange numbers 5 and 6; their participants remain identical. Table 8 retains the same three models and two assistants.

E3.justification: Table 8 expands the reported activation-steering metrics from separate acceptance/refusal rates to include the already-defined operational-safety score and its improvement. Stated sampling, decoding, training, and steering-search settings remain unchanged; no rerun is established.

E4.justification: The model-size/reasoning, post-breach, prompt-design, multi-turn, translation, distributional, and parameter-steering analyses are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or empirical case study is introduced; Table 8 updates an existing mitigation comparison.

E5.justification: Appendix G retains seed 24, and Table 2 retains its average-and-standard-deviation summaries across models. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: In Table 8, Ministral (8B)/medischeduler's steered in-domain acceptance changes from 0.94 to 64.71%, reversing the reported acceptance improvement into a decline. Base/steered OS scores and gains are newly reported for the same six model–assistant pairs. Other matched experiments and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The prompt-laundering and content-equivalence definitions, operational-safety harmonic mean, and activation-vector construction are unchanged. Table 8 applies existing mathematics; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the claimed significance of operational-safety failures by presenting harmless OOD compliance as evidence of lost control and a proxy for broader guardrail failure. The benchmark contributions, mitigation claims, and abstract/conclusion findings otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation connecting out-of-scope responses to enterprise liability and guardrail deactivation, illustrated through the cited Air Canada case. Its new Ethics Statement also identifies multilingual misuse risks from releasing the dataset. These additions are not accompanied by new empirical validation.

D1.justification: v1 provides separate GitHub code and Hugging Face dataset links; v3 supplies a combined code-and-data GitHub link in the abstract and omits the direct dataset link. Implementation details and prompts remain unchanged, while the new Reproducibility Statement restates existing documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds NIST AI Risk Management Framework and Air Canada references, alongside expanded enterprise-risk positioning using OWASP and EU guidance. The technical related-work discussion and relationships to existing attack and steering methods remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction receives limited additions, and acknowledgements, ethics, and reproducibility statements are added after the conclusion. Author affiliations and publication headers change. Most scientific prose and all appendix text are retained.

P2.justification: Table 8 is reorganized into Base/Steered groups with percentage values, OS columns, and an improvement column. The prompt-steering tables swap numbers and positions, Figure 1 moves, and conference headers alter page layout. The underlying figures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 8 makes the joint acceptance/refusal tradeoff easier to assess through explicit OS scores and gains, providing a limited reporting improvement. Enterprise motivation and dataset-misuse concerns are also more explicit. These benefits are modest: the experiments and appendices are otherwise unchanged, and the added inference from harmless OOD compliance to broader guardrail failure remains unvalidated.
